newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close lower on Telekom woes.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close lower on Telekom woes.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed lower on Wednesday, dragged down by selling pressure on Telekom Malaysia, analysts and dealers said.
At the close, the benchmark Composite Index of leading blue-chip stocks shed 2.11 points, or 0.19 percent, at 1,108.25. The index had slumped to 1,103.38 earlier.
"Telekom's fall led the fall in the market in general," said Soh Meng Hui, research manager at K.L. City Securities.
Telekom shares dipped 30 cents to 12.20 ringgit. The company had announced earlier this week it was buying a 20.12 percent stake in a Thai telecommunications firm.
Telekom stock fell on worries its aggressive overseas expansion would impose a drain on the company's cash flow.

Time Engineering also came under pressure earlier after news the company may delay the initial public offering of its unit Time Telekom. The stock ended unchanged at 4.16, after falling to a 12-month low of 3.80.
News of Thailand imposing a ban on repatriation of funds in baht by foreign investors, did not have an impact on the market.
"Our economy is unlike Thailand, I don't think the government will need measures like that to curb speculation," said Phua Lee Kerk, head of research at Jupiter Securities.

The imposition of the ban on baht repatriation from Thailand may have also adversely affected Telekom Malaysia, as the company had just acquired a 20.12 percent stake in local telecommunications firm Samart Corporation Plc.
"It may have been one reason for Telekom's fall, and the market's fall," said Soh.
Telekom has a 10.09 percent weighting on the Composite Index.
Westmont Industries, and Selangor Dredging were the two most active stocks of the day, although dealers said they could not ascertain the reason for the activity.

Suria Capital fell two cents to 3.02 ringgit. The company submitted a proposal to the Malaysian authorities on Tuesday to start talks for a merger with MBf Capital. MBf Capital stock is still suspended, but parent MBf Holdings fell 6.0 cents to 1.32.
On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot June contract closed 11.9 points lower at 1,107.5. No other contracts were traded.
